prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a service counter directly in front of and below the camera wearer (roughly 0.5–1.2 m away in frames 1–3) separating the wearer from three standing people lined up from left to right about 0.4–0.6 m apart and 1.2–2.0 m away in front of a corrugated shutter wall (~2.0–2.8 m away). Across the 5 frames, the foreground counter, terminal screen, cup sealer on the left, and the three people progressively darken from bright/mid-grey to dark grey as the camera wearer retreats and turns leftward toward a bright side counter and wall (~0.5–1.0 m away on the left in frames 4–5), increasing the distance to the left-most person to ~2.5–3.0 m while the middle person steps slightly forward around the right end of the counter (~1.5–1.8 m away). In frames 1–3, the counter surface, POS monitor, straw holder, and the camera wearer's own raised hand at the bottom of frame 3 (~0.3 m away) are within the wearer's arm's reach, while the counter edge and held phones are within arm's reach of the left and middle people, whose lower bodies are occluded behind the counter. The map reveals continuous 3D distance gradients—such as the receding floor plane, the protruding left wall/pillar in frame 4, and the depth gap between the three people and the shutter behind them—more clearly than the wide-angle fisheye RGB alone. However, it is unreliable in frames 4–5 where the left-most person and background shutter merge into nearly black drop-outs, and where small counter items (payment scanner, straw dispenser, black bag) blur into a single smooth surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates up to three standing people in front of the camera wearer (~1.2–3.0 m away, spaced ~0.5 m apart from left to right), along with the counter monitor below the left person (labeled 'laptop' or 'tv' at ~0.8–2.0 m), handheld 'cell phone' masks in frames 1, 2, and 4, and stainless-steel counter surfaces on the lower left of frame 5 (mislabelled as 'laptop'). In frames 1–3, the left person (olive shirt, ~1.2–1.8 m away) and middle person (light green shirt, ~1.3–1.8 m away) stand side by side facing the camera wearer with the counter occluding their legs, while the right-most person (white shirt with '30', ~1.6–2.2 m away) is missing in frame 1, segmented in frames 2–3, and occluded behind the middle person in frames 4–5 as the camera wearer steps back and pans left. The counter screen is within arm's reach of both the camera wearer (in frames 1–3) and the left person, while the segmented cell phones are held directly in front of the middle person's chest in frames 1–2 and on the counter in frame 4. Compared to RGB, the masks clearly delineate individual person boundaries and pinpoint the small handheld phone against the middle person's hands, as well as the partial occlusion of the right-most person behind the middle person in frame 3. However, the map is unreliable across frames: it misses the right-most person in frames 1, 4, and 5, fragments the middle person's lower torso into a separate blue mask in frame 3, misclassifies the POS monitor and metal worktable as 'laptop'/'tv' and a background bag as 'chair', and omits the counter, cup sealer, and the camera wearer's hand in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D upper-body and leg skeletons (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) for subsets of the three people standing 1.2–3.0 m in front of the camera wearer, showing their torso orientations facing generally toward the counter and camera wearer across the sequence. In frame 1 only the middle person (~1.3 m away, right of center) is tracked leaning slightly forward with head keypoints angled toward the counter; in frame 2 only the middle person is tracked standing upright with both magenta hands converged at chest height (~1.4 m away) holding a phone; and in frame 3 both the left person (~1.5 m away, looking down toward his converged magenta hands) and middle person (~1.6 m away, looking toward the left person with his right magenta hand resting on the counter edge) are tracked side by side about 0.5 m apart. As the camera wearer retreats and turns left in frames 4–5, frame 4 shows full-body skeletons including legs for the left person (~2.4 m away, facing the counter with hands near his waist/counter) and the middle person (~1.8 m away, stepping around the right end of the counter with his right magenta hand touching the counter corner), while frame 5 tracks only the middle person (~1.6 m away on the right) turning his head and torso toward the left person across the counter. The skeleton map makes torso orientation, shoulder tilt, head direction, and exact hand placement (holding phones within personal reach or resting on the counter within arm's reach) much easier to read in isolation than in the cluttered, fisheye-distorted RGB frames. However, it is highly incomplete and unreliable for full-scene coverage: it completely fails to detect the right-most person in all five frames, misses the left person in frames 1, 2, and 5, hallucinates unoccluded lower-leg keypoints through the solid counter in frames 2 and 3, and places a detached cluster of magenta hand keypoints below the middle person's waist on the counter in frame 1.
